430.text: OCPs are embedded within the Australian Cancer Plan as national standards for delivery of high- quality, consistent cancer care. Their development is guided by the National Optimal Care Pathways Framework , which provides a consistent approach to prioritisation, development, update and endorsement of OCPs and supports their adoption into health systems.

579.text: Health equity in cancer outcomes is the absence of disparities for people with different levels of social advantage. 1

589.text: Person-centred care means informing and involving people in their care, and respecting and responding to their individual needs, preferences and values, as well as those of their families and carers. 2

598.text: Safe and quality care means delivering the most appropriate and best-value care, while keeping people safe from preventable harm in the delivery of that care. 3

607.text: Multidisciplinary care is an integrated team approach that involves all relevant health professionals discussing all relevant treatment options and making joint recommendations about treatment and supportive care plans that consider the individual characteristics and preferences of the person with cancer. 4

616.text: Supportive care involves prevention and management of the adverse effects of cancer and its treatment, including management of physical and psychological symptoms and side effects across the cancer continuum. Supportive care aims to improve the quality of rehabilitation, secondary cancer prevention, survivorship, and end-of-life care. 5

625.text: Navigation and care coordination are related person-centred interventions that aim to empower patients, families and carers affected by cancer to facilitate safe and timely access to optimal cancer-related care and support. 6

643.text: Research and clinical trials generate evidence to improve understanding of cancer and to accelerate progress in prevention, detection, diagnosis, treatment, supportive care, survivorship care, palliative and end-of-life care. 8
